cond_0001.intro:
The Research Associate I (RA I) works to meet deadlines and operates proactively and collaboratively in a team in support of research and development activities. Tasks will focus on molecular and microbiological experiments and procedures (e.g., nucleic acid extraction, serial dilution, PCR, bacterial and fungal culture, etc.) with associated collection, analysis, verification and recording of data in accordance with established protocols and work instruction documents, regulations, safety requirements, and the quality system. Work is primarily collaborative and requires the ability to communicate and coordinate with peers and supervisor(s) effectively and respectfully.
The position requires basic laboratory technical skills, organizational skills, attention to detail, critical thinking, troubleshooting and problem-solving, and a dedication to the mission and goals of the department and [Company name masked]. A Research Associate I may receive general or detailed instruction and direct supervision on general work, new procedures, and assignments.
cond_0001.responsibilities:
Assists with stocking project-specific laboratory supplies, including inventorying stock. Act as a good lab citizen and team member. Coordinate and collaborate within and across teams and functional groups for routine lab activities, cleaning, equipment use, specific assigned tasks and projects, and sharing of knowledge, skills, and ideas. Work in a Biosafety level 2/2+ environment with potentially pathogenic microbes, patient samples, and body fluids using sterile technique for contamination and infection control. Ensure data integrity and accurate record-keeping by collecting, recording (in an electronic laboratory notebook and/or study worksheets), analyzing and verifying data in compliance with company standard operating procedures, work instruction documents, and study protocols. Use and maintain laboratory equipment, supplies/inventory, and workspaces according to operational, quality, and safety requirements as outlined in protocols, standard operating procedures, and work instruction documents. Perform routine calculations and laboratory techniques including solution formulation, microbial culture and enumeration, nucleic acid extraction and quantification, real-time and/or digital PCR, as well as basic statistical analyses. Execute study protocols and contribute to protocol and process development, optimization, and/or revision. Conduct routine data analysis under supervision. Communicate data and analyses in written reports and oral presentations to peers and supervisors, commensurate with job level. Contribute to the writing of study reports. Perform all work in compliance with [Company name masked] corporate policies and within the guidelines of the Quality Management System. Perform other duties as assigned.
Performs work under direct supervision. Handles basic issues and problems and refers more complex issues to higher-level staff.
cond_0001.requirements:
Minimum Requirements
Bachelor's degree in a scientific discipline.
A minimum of six months' experience in an academic, industry, or healthcare laboratory.
Basic competence in laboratory practices including pipetting, handling biological and chemical materials, sterile technique and contamination control, and basic concentration and statistical calculations.
Detail-oriented in executing work and in record keeping.
Strong oral and written communication skills.
Ability to follow rules and regulations.
Comfortable working with human specimens and fluids (blood, stool, sputum, etc.).
Comfortable working with biosafety level 2 pathogens.
Preferred Requirements
Beginning to working knowledge of current and evolving microbiology and molecular biology principles, tools, and techniques relevant to developing diagnostic tests for infectious diseases.
Basic competence with Microsoft Office (Outlook, Excel, PowerPoint, and Word).
Comfortable working in a dynamic environment where priorities sometimes change on short notice.
Aptitude for critical thinking and problem-solving.
Physical Requirements
Must be able to lift and safely maneuver 40 lbs. Manual and visual dexterity to handle small tubes and manipulate very small volumes; reasonable accommodations are applicable. Must be able to wear personal protective equipment, including a lab coat, disposable gloves, face mask, and safety glasses, as needed. Comfortable working with cleaning products such as bleach.

Tasks will focus on molecular and microbiological experiments and procedures (e.g., nucleic acid extraction, serial dilution, PCR, bacterial and fungal culture, etc.) with associated collection, analysis, verification and recording of data in accordance with established protocols and work instruction documents, regulations, safety requirements, and the quality system. Work is primarily collaborative and requires the ability to communicate and coordinate with peers and supervisor(s) effectively and respectfully.
The position requires basic laboratory technical skills, organizational skills, attention to detail, critical thinking, troubleshooting and problem-solving, and a dedication to the mission and goals of the department and [Company name masked]. A Research Associate I may receive general or detailed instruction and direct supervision on general work, new procedures, and assignments.
cond_0037.responsibilities:
Assists with stocking project-specific laboratory supplies, including inventorying stock. Act as a good lab citizen and team member. Coordinate and collaborate within and across teams and functional groups for routine lab activities, cleaning, equipment use, specific assigned tasks and projects, and sharing of knowledge, skills, and ideas. Work in a Biosafety level 2/2+ environment with potentially pathogenic microbes, patient samples, and body fluids using sterile technique for contamination and infection control. Ensure data integrity and accurate record-keeping by collecting, recording (in an electronic laboratory notebook and/or study worksheets), analyzing and verifying data in compliance with company standard operating procedures, work instruction documents, and study protocols. Use and maintain laboratory equipment, supplies/inventory, and workspaces according to operational, quality, and safety requirements as outlined in protocols, standard operating procedures, and work instruction documents. Perform routine calculations and laboratory techniques including solution formulation, microbial culture and enumeration, nucleic acid extraction and quantification, real-time and/or digital PCR, as well as basic statistical analyses. Execute study protocols and contribute to protocol and process development, optimization, and/or revision. Conduct routine data analysis under supervision. Communicate data and analyses in written reports and oral presentations to peers and supervisors, commensurate with job level. Contribute to the writing of study reports. Perform all work in compliance with [Company name masked] corporate policies and within the guidelines of the Quality Management System. Perform other duties as assigned.
Performs work under direct supervision. Handles basic issues and problems and refers more complex issues to higher-level staff.
cond_0037.requirements:
Minimum Requirements
Bachelor's degree in a scientific discipline.
A minimum of six months' experience in an academic, industry, or healthcare laboratory.
Basic competence in laboratory practices including pipetting, handling biological and chemical materials, sterile technique and contamination control, and basic concentration and statistical calculations.
Detail-oriented in executing work and in record keeping.
Strong oral and written communication skills.
Ability to follow rules and regulations.
Comfortable working with human specimens and fluids (blood, stool, sputum, etc.).
Comfortable working with biosafety level 2 pathogens.
Preferred Requirements
Beginning to working knowledge of current and evolving microbiology and molecular biology principles, tools, and techniques relevant to developing diagnostic tests for infectious diseases.
Basic competence with Microsoft Office (Outlook, Excel, PowerPoint, and Word).
Comfortable working in a dynamic environment where priorities sometimes change on short notice.
Aptitude for critical thinking and problem-solving.
Physical Requirements
Must be able to lift and safely maneuver 40 lbs. Manual and visual dexterity to handle small tubes and manipulate very small volumes; reasonable accommodations are applicable. Must be able to wear personal protective equipment, including a lab coat, disposable gloves, face mask, and safety glasses, as needed. Comfortable working with cleaning products such as bleach.

Tasks will focus on molecular and microbiological experiments and procedures (e.g., nucleic acid extraction, serial dilution, PCR, bacterial and fungal culture, etc.) with associated collection, analysis, verification and recording of data in accordance with established protocols and work instruction documents, regulations, safety requirements, and the quality system. Work is primarily collaborative and requires the ability to communicate and coordinate with peers and supervisor(s) effectively and respectfully.
The position requires basic laboratory technical skills, organizational skills, attention to detail, critical thinking, troubleshooting and problem-solving, and a dedication to the mission and goals of the department and [Company name masked]. A Research Associate I may receive general or detailed instruction and direct supervision on general work, new procedures, and assignments.
cond_0146.responsibilities:
Assists with stocking project-specific laboratory supplies, including inventorying stock. Act as a good lab citizen and team member. Coordinate and collaborate within and across teams and functional groups for routine lab activities, cleaning, equipment use, specific assigned tasks and projects, and sharing of knowledge, skills, and ideas. Work in a Biosafety level 2/2+ environment with potentially pathogenic microbes, patient samples, and body fluids using sterile technique for contamination and infection control. Ensure data integrity and accurate record-keeping by collecting, recording (in an electronic laboratory notebook and/or study worksheets), analyzing and verifying data in compliance with company standard operating procedures, work instruction documents, and study protocols. Use and maintain laboratory equipment, supplies/inventory, and workspaces according to operational, quality, and safety requirements as outlined in protocols, standard operating procedures, and work instruction documents. Perform routine calculations and laboratory techniques including solution formulation, microbial culture and enumeration, nucleic acid extraction and quantification, real-time and/or digital PCR, as well as basic statistical analyses. Execute study protocols and contribute to protocol and process development, optimization, and/or revision. Conduct routine data analysis under supervision. Communicate data and analyses in written reports and oral presentations to peers and supervisors, commensurate with job level. Contribute to the writing of study reports. Perform all work in compliance with [Company name masked] corporate policies and within the guidelines of the Quality Management System. Perform other duties as assigned.
Performs work under direct supervision. Handles basic issues and problems and refers more complex issues to higher-level staff.
cond_0146.requirements:
Minimum Requirements
Bachelor's degree in a scientific discipline required; advanced degree strongly preferred.
Minimum six months of demonstrated laboratory experience in an academic, industry, or healthcare setting.
Proven competence in laboratory practices including pipetting, handling biological and chemical materials, sterile technique and contamination control, and basic concentration and statistical calculations.
Solid understanding of current and evolving microbiology and molecular biology principles, tools, and techniques relevant to developing diagnostic tests for infectious diseases.
Strong command of Microsoft Office (Outlook, Excel, PowerPoint, and Word).
Exceptional attention to detail in executing work and in record keeping.
Exceptional oral and written communication skills.
Ability to follow rules and regulations.
Preferred Requirements
Demonstrated aptitude for critical thinking and problem-solving in a laboratory context.
Proven ability to work effectively when priorities shift on short notice.
Demonstrated comfort working with human specimens and fluids (blood, stool, sputum, etc.).
Demonstrated comfort working with biosafety level 2 pathogens.
Physical Requirements
Must be able to lift and safely maneuver 40 lbs. Manual and visual dexterity to handle small tubes and manipulate very small volumes; reasonable accommodations are applicable. Must be able to wear personal protective equipment, including a lab coat, disposable gloves, face mask, and safety glasses, as needed. Comfortable working with cleaning products such as bleach.

cond_0170.intro:
We are looking for a Research Associate I to join our team at [Company name masked].
The Research Associate I (RA I) takes ownership of meeting deadlines and operates proactively within a team to advance research and development activities. Tasks will focus on molecular and microbiological experiments and procedures (e.g., nucleic acid extraction, serial dilution, PCR, bacterial and fungal culture, etc.) with associated collection, analysis, verification and recording of data in accordance with established protocols and work instruction documents, regulations, safety requirements, and the quality system. Work requires the ability to communicate and coordinate with peers and supervisor(s) effectively and respectfully.
The position requires basic laboratory technical skills, organizational skills, attention to detail, critical thinking, troubleshooting and problem-solving, and a dedication to the mission and goals of the department and [Company name masked]. A Research Associate I may receive general or detailed instruction and direct supervision on general work, new procedures, and assignments.
cond_0170.responsibilities:
Manage stocking of project-specific laboratory supplies, including inventorying stock. Act as a good lab citizen and team member. Lead coordination and collaboration within and across teams and functional groups for routine lab activities, cleaning, equipment use, specific assigned tasks and projects, and sharing of knowledge, skills, and ideas. Work in a Biosafety level 2/2+ environment with potentially pathogenic microbes, patient samples, and body fluids using sterile technique for contamination and infection control. Ensure data integrity and accurate record-keeping by collecting, recording (in an electronic laboratory notebook and/or study worksheets), analyzing and verifying data in compliance with company standard operating procedures, work instruction documents, and study protocols. Use and maintain laboratory equipment, supplies/inventory, and workspaces according to operational, quality, and safety requirements as outlined in protocols, standard operating procedures, and work instruction documents. Execute routine calculations and laboratory techniques including solution formulation, microbial culture and enumeration, nucleic acid extraction and quantification, real-time and/or digital PCR, as well as basic statistical analyses. Execute study protocols and take initiative in protocol and process development, optimization, and/or revision. Conduct routine data analysis under supervision. Deliver data and analyses in written reports and oral presentations to peers and supervisors, commensurate with job level. Contribute to the writing of study reports. Perform all work in compliance with [Company name masked] corporate policies and within the guidelines of the Quality Management System. Perform other duties as assigned.
Performs work under direct supervision. Handles basic issues and problems and refers more complex issues to higher-level staff.
cond_0170.requirements:
Minimum Requirements
Bachelor's degree in a scientific discipline.
A minimum of six months' experience in an academic, industry, or healthcare laboratory.
Basic competence in laboratory practices including pipetting, handling biological and chemical materials, sterile technique and contamination control, and basic concentration and statistical calculations.
Detail-oriented in executing work and in record keeping.
Strong oral and written communication skills.
Ability to follow rules and regulations.
Comfortable working with human specimens and fluids (blood, stool, sputum, etc.).
Comfortable working with biosafety level 2 pathogens.
Preferred Requirements
Beginning to working knowledge of current and evolving microbiology and molecular biology principles, tools, and techniques relevant to developing diagnostic tests for infectious diseases.
Basic competence with Microsoft Office (Outlook, Excel, PowerPoint, and Word).
Comfortable working in a dynamic environment where priorities sometimes change on short notice.
Aptitude for critical thinking and problem-solving.
Physical Requirements
Must be able to lift and safely maneuver 40 lbs. Manual and visual dexterity to handle small tubes and manipulate very small volumes; reasonable accommodations are applicable. Must be able to wear personal protective equipment, including a lab coat, disposable gloves, face mask, and safety glasses, as needed. Comfortable working with cleaning products such as bleach.

cond_0195.intro:
The Research Associate I (RA I) works to meet deadlines and operates collaboratively and proactively in a team, supporting research and development activities. Tasks focus on molecular and microbiological experiments and procedures (e.g., nucleic acid extraction, serial dilution, PCR, bacterial and fungal culture, etc.) with associated collection, analysis, verification, and recording of data in accordance with established protocols and work instruction documents, regulations, safety requirements, and the quality system. A large part of the role involves regular communication and coordination with peers and supervisors, and the work is primarily collaborative in nature.
The position requires basic laboratory technical skills, organizational skills, attention to detail, critical thinking, troubleshooting and problem-solving, and a dedication to the mission and goals of the department and [Company name masked]. A Research Associate I may receive general or detailed instruction and direct supervision on general work, new procedures, and assignments.
cond_0195.responsibilities:
Assists with stocking project-specific laboratory supplies, including inventorying stock. Act as a good lab citizen and team member. Actively coordinate and collaborate within and across teams and functional groups for routine lab activities, cleaning, equipment use, specific assigned tasks and projects, and sharing of knowledge, skills, and ideas. Work in a Biosafety level 2/2+ environment with potentially pathogenic microbes, patient samples, and body fluids using sterile technique for contamination and infection control. Ensure data integrity and accurate record-keeping by collecting, recording (in an electronic laboratory notebook and/or study worksheets), analyzing, and verifying data in compliance with company standard operating procedures, work instruction documents, and study protocols. Use and maintain laboratory equipment, supplies/inventory, and workspaces according to operational, quality, and safety requirements as outlined in protocols, standard operating procedures, and work instruction documents. Perform routine calculations and laboratory techniques including solution formulation, microbial culture and enumeration, nucleic acid extraction and quantification, real-time and/or digital PCR, as well as basic statistical analyses. Execute study protocols and actively contribute to protocol and process development, optimization, and/or revision. Conduct routine data analysis under supervision. Communicate data and analyses clearly in written reports and oral presentations to peers and supervisors, walking them through findings and handling questions commensurate with job level. Contribute to the writing of study reports. Perform all work in compliance with [Company name masked] corporate policies and within the guidelines of the Quality Management System. Perform other duties as assigned.
Performs work under direct supervision. Handles basic issues and problems and refers more complex issues to higher-level staff.
cond_0195.requirements:

A minimum of six months' experience in an academic, industry, or healthcare laboratory.
Beginning to working knowledge of current and evolving microbiology and molecular biology principles, tools, and techniques relevant to developing diagnostic tests for infectious diseases.
Detail-oriented in executing work and in record keeping.
Strong oral and written communication skills, including the ability to clearly explain results and clarify findings with peers and supervisors.
Basic competence in laboratory practices including pipetting, handling biological and chemical materials, sterile technique and contamination control, and basic concentration and statistical calculations.
Basic competence with Microsoft Office (Outlook, Excel, PowerPoint, and Word).
Comfortable working in an environment where priorities sometimes change on short notice.
Comfortable working with human specimens and fluids (blood, stool, sputum, etc.).

Tasks focus on molecular and microbiological experiments and procedures (e.g., nucleic acid extraction, serial dilution, PCR, bacterial and fungal culture, etc.) with associated collection, analysis, verification, and recording of data in accordance with established protocols and work instruction documents, regulations, safety requirements, and the quality system. A large part of the role involves regular communication and coordination with peers and supervisors, and the work is primarily collaborative in nature.
The position requires basic laboratory technical skills, organizational skills, attention to detail, critical thinking, troubleshooting and problem-solving, and a dedication to the mission and goals of the department and [Company name masked]. A Research Associate I may receive general or detailed instruction and direct supervision on general work, new procedures, and assignments.
cond_0249.responsibilities:
Assists with stocking project-specific laboratory supplies, including inventorying stock. Act as a good lab citizen and team member. Actively coordinate and collaborate within and across teams and functional groups for routine lab activities, cleaning, equipment use, specific assigned tasks and projects, and sharing of knowledge, skills, and ideas. Work in a Biosafety level 2/2+ environment with potentially pathogenic microbes, patient samples, and body fluids using sterile technique for contamination and infection control. Ensure data integrity and accurate record-keeping by collecting, recording (in an electronic laboratory notebook and/or study worksheets), analyzing, and verifying data in compliance with company standard operating procedures, work instruction documents, and study protocols. Use and maintain laboratory equipment, supplies/inventory, and workspaces according to operational, quality, and safety requirements as outlined in protocols, standard operating procedures, and work instruction documents. Perform routine calculations and laboratory techniques including solution formulation, microbial culture and enumeration, nucleic acid extraction and quantification, real-time and/or digital PCR, as well as basic statistical analyses. Execute study protocols and actively contribute to protocol and process development, optimization, and/or revision. Conduct routine data analysis under supervision. Communicate data and analyses clearly in written reports and oral presentations to peers and supervisors, walking them through findings and handling questions commensurate with job level. Contribute to the writing of study reports. Perform all work in compliance with [Company name masked] corporate policies and within the guidelines of the Quality Management System. Perform other duties as assigned.
Performs work under direct supervision. Handles basic issues and problems and refers more complex issues to higher-level staff.
cond_0249.requirements:
Bachelor's degree in a scientific discipline.
A minimum of six months' experience in an academic, industry, or healthcare laboratory.
Beginning to working knowledge of current and evolving microbiology and molecular biology principles, tools, and techniques relevant to developing diagnostic tests for infectious diseases.
Detail-oriented in executing work and in record keeping.
Strong oral and written communication skills, including the ability to clearly explain results and clarify findings with peers and supervisors.
Basic competence in laboratory practices including pipetting, handling biological and chemical materials, sterile technique and contamination control, and basic concentration and statistical calculations.
Basic competence with Microsoft Office (Outlook, Excel, PowerPoint, and Word).
Comfortable working in an environment where priorities sometimes change on short notice.
Comfortable working with human specimens and fluids (blood, stool, sputum, etc.).
Comfortable working with biosafety level 2 pathogens.
Aptitude for critical thinking and problem-solving.
Ability to follow rules and regulations.
Must be able to lift and safely maneuver 40 lbs. Manual and visual dexterity to handle small tubes and manipulate very small volumes; reasonable accommodations are applicable. Must be able to wear personal protective equipment, including a lab coat, disposable gloves, face mask, and safety glasses, as needed. Comfortable working with cleaning products such as bleach.
cond_0249.values: We value delivering results to a high standard and taking pride in work done well. We aim to be defined by quality, consistency, and strong performance.

Tasks will focus on molecular and microbiological experiments and procedures (e.g., nucleic acid extraction, serial dilution, PCR, bacterial and fungal culture, etc.) with associated collection, analysis, verification and recording of data in accordance with established protocols and work instruction documents, regulations, safety requirements, and the quality system. Work is primarily collaborative and requires the ability to communicate and coordinate with peers and supervisor(s) effectively and respectfully.
The position requires basic laboratory technical skills, organizational skills, attention to detail, critical thinking, troubleshooting and problem-solving, and a dedication to the mission and goals of the department and [Company name masked]. A Research Associate I may receive general or detailed instruction and direct supervision on general work, new procedures, and assignments.
cond_0264.responsibilities:
Assists with stocking project-specific laboratory supplies, including inventorying stock. Act as a good lab citizen and team member. Coordinate and collaborate within and across teams and functional groups for routine lab activities, cleaning, equipment use, specific assigned tasks and projects, and sharing of knowledge, skills, and ideas. Work in a Biosafety level 2/2+ environment with potentially pathogenic microbes, patient samples, and body fluids using sterile technique for contamination and infection control. Ensure data integrity and accurate record-keeping by collecting, recording (in an electronic laboratory notebook and/or study worksheets), analyzing and verifying data in compliance with company standard operating procedures, work instruction documents, and study protocols. Use and maintain laboratory equipment, supplies/inventory, and workspaces according to operational, quality, and safety requirements as outlined in protocols, standard operating procedures, and work instruction documents. Perform routine calculations and laboratory techniques including solution formulation, microbial culture and enumeration, nucleic acid extraction and quantification, real-time and/or digital PCR, as well as basic statistical analyses. Execute study protocols and contribute to protocol and process development, optimization, and/or revision. Conduct routine data analysis under supervision. Communicate data and analyses in written reports and oral presentations to peers and supervisors, commensurate with job level. Contribute to the writing of study reports. Perform all work in compliance with [Company name masked] corporate policies and within the guidelines of the Quality Management System. Perform other duties as assigned.
Performs work under direct supervision. Handles basic issues and problems and refers more complex issues to higher-level staff.
cond_0264.requirements:
Bachelor's degree in a scientific discipline, or equivalent practical experience.
Around six months of experience in an academic, industry, or healthcare laboratory, or an equivalent combination of education and training.
Some background in current and evolving microbiology and molecular biology principles, tools, and techniques relevant to developing diagnostic tests for infectious diseases — this knowledge can continue to develop on the job.
Attention to detail in executing work and in record keeping.
Ability to communicate effectively in both oral and written forms.
Familiarity with laboratory practices including pipetting, handling biological and chemical materials, sterile technique and contamination control, and basic concentration and statistical calculations.
Familiarity with Microsoft Office (Outlook, Excel, PowerPoint, and Word).
Willingness to work in an environment where priorities sometimes shift on short notice.
Comfortable working with human specimens and fluids (blood, stool, sputum, etc.).
Comfortable working with biosafety level 2 pathogens.
Openness to critical thinking and problem-solving as part of daily work.
Ability to follow rules and regulations.
Physical Requirements
Must be able to lift and safely maneuver 40 lbs. Manual and visual dexterity to handle small tubes and manipulate very small volumes; reasonable accommodations are applicable. Must be able to wear personal protective equipment, including a lab coat, disposable gloves, face mask, and safety glasses, as needed. Comfortable working with cleaning products such as bleach.

Tasks will focus on molecular and microbiological experiments and procedures (e.g., nucleic acid extraction, serial dilution, PCR, bacterial and fungal culture, etc.) with associated collection, analysis, verification and recording of data in accordance with established protocols and work instruction documents, regulations, safety requirements, and the quality system. Work is primarily collaborative and requires the ability to communicate and coordinate with peers and supervisor(s) effectively and respectfully.
The position requires basic laboratory technical skills, organizational skills, attention to detail, critical thinking, troubleshooting and problem-solving, and a dedication to the mission and goals of the department and [Company name masked]. A Research Associate I may receive general or detailed instruction and direct supervision on general work, new procedures, and assignments.
cond_0390.responsibilities:
Assists with stocking project-specific laboratory supplies, including inventorying stock. Act as a good lab citizen and team member. Coordinate and collaborate within and across teams and functional groups for routine lab activities, cleaning, equipment use, specific assigned tasks and projects, and sharing of knowledge, skills, and ideas. Work in a Biosafety level 2/2+ environment with potentially pathogenic microbes, patient samples, and body fluids using sterile technique for contamination and infection control. Ensure data integrity and accurate record-keeping by collecting, recording (in an electronic laboratory notebook and/or study worksheets), analyzing and verifying data in compliance with company standard operating procedures, work instruction documents, and study protocols. Use and maintain laboratory equipment, supplies/inventory, and workspaces according to operational, quality, and safety requirements as outlined in protocols, standard operating procedures, and work instruction documents. Perform routine calculations and laboratory techniques including solution formulation, microbial culture and enumeration, nucleic acid extraction and quantification, real-time and/or digital PCR, as well as basic statistical analyses. Execute study protocols and contribute to protocol and process development, optimization, and/or revision. Conduct routine data analysis under supervision. Communicate data and analyses in written reports and oral presentations to peers and supervisors, commensurate with job level. Contribute to the writing of study reports. Perform all work in compliance with [Company name masked] corporate policies and within the guidelines of the Quality Management System. Perform other duties as assigned.
Performs work under direct supervision. Handles basic issues and problems and refers more complex issues to higher-level staff.
cond_0390.requirements:
Bachelor's degree in a scientific discipline, or equivalent practical experience.
Around six months of experience in an academic, industry, or healthcare laboratory, or an equivalent combination of education and training.
Some background in current and evolving microbiology and molecular biology principles, tools, and techniques relevant to developing diagnostic tests for infectious diseases — this knowledge can continue to develop on the job.
Attention to detail in executing work and in record keeping.
Ability to communicate effectively in both oral and written forms.
Familiarity with laboratory practices including pipetting, handling biological and chemical materials, sterile technique and contamination control, and basic concentration and statistical calculations.
Familiarity with Microsoft Office (Outlook, Excel, PowerPoint, and Word).
Willingness to work in an environment where priorities sometimes shift on short notice.
Comfortable working with human specimens and fluids (blood, stool, sputum, etc.).
Comfortable working with biosafety level 2 pathogens.
Openness to critical thinking and problem-solving as part of daily work.
Ability to follow rules and regulations.
Physical Requirements
Must be able to lift and safely maneuver 40 lbs. Manual and visual dexterity to handle small tubes and manipulate very small volumes; reasonable accommodations are applicable. Must be able to wear personal protective equipment, including a lab coat, disposable gloves, face mask, and safety glasses, as needed. Comfortable working with cleaning products such as bleach.
cond_0390.values: We value delivering results to a high standard and taking pride in work done well. We aim to be defined by quality, consistency, and strong performance.

The Research Associate I (RA I) works to meet deadlines and operates proactively and collaboratively in a team in support of research and development activities. Tasks will focus on molecular and microbiological experiments and procedures (e.g., nucleic acid extraction, serial dilution, PCR, bacterial and fungal culture, etc.) with associated collection, analysis, verification and recording of data in accordance with established protocols and work instruction documents, regulations, safety requirements, and the quality system. Work is primarily collaborative and requires the ability to communicate and coordinate with peers and supervisor(s) effectively and respectfully.
The position requires basic laboratory technical skills, organizational skills, attention to detail, critical thinking, troubleshooting and problem-solving, and a dedication to the mission and goals of the department and [Company name masked]. A Research Associate I may receive general or detailed instruction and direct supervision on general work, new procedures, and assignments.
cond_0433.responsibilities:
Assists with stocking project-specific laboratory supplies, including inventorying stock. Act as a good lab citizen and team member. Coordinate and collaborate within and across teams and functional groups for routine lab activities, cleaning, equipment use, specific assigned tasks and projects, and sharing of knowledge, skills, and ideas. Work in a Biosafety level 2/2+ environment with potentially pathogenic microbes, patient samples, and body fluids using sterile technique for contamination and infection control. Ensure data integrity and accurate record-keeping by collecting, recording (in an electronic laboratory notebook and/or study worksheets), analyzing and verifying data in compliance with company standard operating procedures, work instruction documents, and study protocols. Use and maintain laboratory equipment, supplies/inventory, and workspaces according to operational, quality, and safety requirements as outlined in protocols, standard operating procedures, and work instruction documents. Perform routine calculations and laboratory techniques including solution formulation, microbial culture and enumeration, nucleic acid extraction and quantification, real-time and/or digital PCR, as well as basic statistical analyses. Execute study protocols and contribute to protocol and process development, optimization, and/or revision. Conduct routine data analysis under supervision. Communicate data and analyses in written reports and oral presentations to peers and supervisors, commensurate with job level. Contribute to the writing of study reports. Perform all work in compliance with [Company name masked] corporate policies and within the guidelines of the Quality Management System. Perform other duties as assigned.
Performs work under direct supervision. Handles basic issues and problems and refers more complex issues to higher-level staff.
cond_0433.requirements:
Minimum Requirements
Bachelor's degree in a scientific discipline.
A minimum of six months' experience in an academic, industry, or healthcare laboratory.
Basic competence in laboratory practices including pipetting, handling biological and chemical materials, sterile technique and contamination control, and basic concentration and statistical calculations.
Detail-oriented in executing work and in record keeping.
Strong oral and written communication skills.
Ability to follow rules and regulations.
Comfortable working with human specimens and fluids (blood, stool, sputum, etc.).
Comfortable working with biosafety level 2 pathogens.
Preferred Requirements
Beginning to working knowledge of current and evolving microbiology and molecular biology principles, tools, and techniques relevant to developing diagnostic tests for infectious diseases.
Basic competence with Microsoft Office (Outlook, Excel, PowerPoint, and Word).
Comfortable working in a dynamic environment where priorities sometimes change on short notice.
Aptitude for critical thinking and problem-solving.
Physical Requirements
Must be able to lift and safely maneuver 40 lbs. Manual and visual dexterity to handle small tubes and manipulate very small volumes; reasonable accommodations are applicable. Must be able to wear personal protective equipment, including a lab coat, disposable gloves, face mask, and safety glasses, as needed. Comfortable working with cleaning products such as bleach.

Tasks will focus on molecular and microbiological experiments and procedures (e.g., nucleic acid extraction, serial dilution, PCR, bacterial and fungal culture, etc.) with associated collection, analysis, verification and recording of data in accordance with established protocols and work instruction documents, regulations, safety requirements, and the quality system. Work is primarily collaborative and requires the ability to communicate and coordinate with peers and supervisor(s) effectively and respectfully.
The position requires basic laboratory technical skills, organizational skills, attention to detail, critical thinking, troubleshooting and problem-solving, and a dedication to the mission and goals of the department and [Company name masked]. A Research Associate I may receive general or detailed instruction and direct supervision on general work, new procedures, and assignments. People usually grow into this role over time as they build experience with molecular and microbiological lab work.
cond_0455.responsibilities:
Assists with stocking project-specific laboratory supplies, including inventorying stock. Act as a good lab citizen and team member. Coordinate and collaborate within and across teams and functional groups for routine lab activities, cleaning, equipment use, specific assigned tasks and projects, and sharing of knowledge, skills, and ideas. Work in a Biosafety level 2/2+ environment with potentially pathogenic microbes, patient samples, and body fluids using sterile technique for contamination and infection control. Ensure data integrity and accurate record-keeping by collecting, recording (in an electronic laboratory notebook and/or study worksheets), analyzing and verifying data in compliance with company standard operating procedures, work instruction documents, and study protocols. Use and maintain laboratory equipment, supplies/inventory, and workspaces according to operational, quality, and safety requirements as outlined in protocols, standard operating procedures, and work instruction documents. Perform routine calculations and laboratory techniques including solution formulation, microbial culture and enumeration, nucleic acid extraction and quantification, real-time and/or digital PCR, as well as basic statistical analyses. Execute study protocols and contribute to protocol and process development, optimization, and/or revision. Conduct routine data analysis under supervision. Communicate data and analyses in written reports and oral presentations to peers and supervisors, commensurate with job level. Contribute to the writing of study reports. Perform all work in compliance with [Company name masked] corporate policies and within the guidelines of the Quality Management System. Perform other duties as assigned.
Performs work under direct supervision. Handles basic issues and problems and refers more complex issues to higher-level staff.
cond_0455.requirements:
Minimum Requirements
Bachelor's degree in a scientific discipline.
A minimum of six months' experience in an academic, industry, or healthcare laboratory.
Basic competence in laboratory practices including pipetting, handling biological and chemical materials, sterile technique and contamination control, and basic concentration and statistical calculations.
Detail-oriented in executing work and in record keeping.
Strong oral and written communication skills.
Ability to follow rules and regulations.
Must be able to lift and safely maneuver 40 lbs. Manual and visual dexterity to handle small tubes and manipulate very small volumes; reasonable accommodations are applicable. Must be able to wear personal protective equipment, including a lab coat, disposable gloves, face mask, and safety glasses, as needed. Comfortable working with cleaning products such as bleach.
Preferred Requirements
Beginning to working knowledge of current and evolving microbiology and molecular biology principles, tools, and techniques relevant to developing diagnostic tests for infectious diseases.
Basic competence with Microsoft Office (Outlook, Excel, PowerPoint, and Word).
Comfortable working in a dynamic environment where priorities sometimes change on short notice.
Comfortable working with human specimens and fluids (blood, stool, sputum, etc.).
Comfortable working with biosafety level 2 pathogens.
Aptitude for critical thinking and problem-solving.

Tasks will focus on molecular and microbiological experiments and procedures (e.g., nucleic acid extraction, serial dilution, PCR, bacterial and fungal culture, etc.) with associated collection, analysis, verification and recording of data in accordance with established protocols and work instruction documents, regulations, safety requirements, and the quality system. Work is primarily collaborative and requires the ability to communicate and coordinate with peers and supervisor(s) effectively and respectfully.
The position requires basic laboratory technical skills, organizational skills, attention to detail, critical thinking, troubleshooting and problem-solving, and a dedication to the mission and goals of the department and [Company name masked]. A Research Associate I may receive general or detailed instruction and direct supervision on general work, new procedures, and assignments.
cond_0478.responsibilities:
Assists with stocking project-specific laboratory supplies, including inventorying stock. Act as a good lab citizen and team member. Coordinate and collaborate within and across teams and functional groups for routine lab activities, cleaning, equipment use, specific assigned tasks and projects, and sharing of knowledge, skills, and ideas. Work in a Biosafety level 2/2+ environment with potentially pathogenic microbes, patient samples, and body fluids using sterile technique for contamination and infection control. Ensure data integrity and accurate record-keeping by collecting, recording (in an electronic laboratory notebook and/or study worksheets), analyzing and verifying data in compliance with company standard operating procedures, work instruction documents, and study protocols. Use and maintain laboratory equipment, supplies/inventory, and workspaces according to operational, quality, and safety requirements as outlined in protocols, standard operating procedures, and work instruction documents. Perform routine calculations and laboratory techniques including solution formulation, microbial culture and enumeration, nucleic acid extraction and quantification, real-time and/or digital PCR, as well as basic statistical analyses. Execute study protocols and contribute to protocol and process development, optimization, and/or revision. Conduct routine data analysis under supervision. Communicate data and analyses in written reports and oral presentations to peers and supervisors, commensurate with job level. Contribute to the writing of study reports. Perform all work in compliance with [Company name masked] corporate policies and within the guidelines of the Quality Management System. Perform other duties as assigned.
Performs work under direct supervision. Handles basic issues and problems and refers more complex issues to higher-level staff.
cond_0478.requirements:
Bachelor's degree in a scientific discipline.
A minimum of six months' experience in an academic, industry, or healthcare laboratory.
Has beginning to working knowledge of current and evolving microbiology and molecular biology principles, tools, and techniques relevant to developing diagnostic tests for infectious diseases.
Detail-oriented in executing work and in record keeping.
Strong oral and written communication skills.
Basic competence in laboratory practices including pipetting, handling biological and chemical materials, sterile technique and contamination control, and basic concentration and statistical calculations.
Basic competence with Microsoft Office (Outlook, Excel, PowerPoint, and Word).
Comfortable working in a dynamic environment where priorities sometimes change on short notice.
Comfortable working with human specimens and fluids (blood, stool, sputum, etc.).
Comfortable working with biosafety level 2 pathogens.
Aptitude for critical thinking and problem-solving.
Ability to follow rules and regulations.
Must be able to lift and safely maneuver 40 lbs. Manual and visual dexterity to handle small tubes and manipulate very small volumes; reasonable accommodations are applicable. Must be able to wear personal protective equipment, including a lab coat, disposable gloves, face mask, and safety glasses, as needed. Comfortable working with cleaning products such as bleach.
